Subject: Kyra Health — Private Install Transition & Connectivity Plan

Hi Ellen and Rajiv —

Congrats on signing the private deployment! I'm Mina, your Customer Success Manager at Redwood. This thread is to kick off the implementation planning and to align on connectivity model (VPC peering vs private endpoints vs on-prem package), timeline, and ownership.

Attachments included: kyra_network_diagram_v1.pdf (your internal network), rdw-onprem-pack-checklist.xlsx (our standard install checklist).

Proposed agenda for a 60-minute kickoff:
- Introductions & roles (5m)
- Connectivity & security model decision (15m)
- Network configuration details: CIDRs, NAT/static IPs, firewall rules, routes (20m)
- On-prem package install plan & acceptance tests (10m)
- Next steps & milestones (10m)

Can you confirm:
1) Which connectivity model you prefer (VPC peering, managed private endpoints, or receiving the on-prem package behind your firewall)?
2) Who owns network changes and when can we schedule a technical deep dive (next week availability)?

I'll loop in Dev (solutions) and Laura (implementation lead) to coordinate the runbook and schedule.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Thanks Mina —

Glad to get this moving. A few quick answers and clarifying questions from our side:
- Preference: We lean toward VPC peering between our AWS account and Redwood's dedicated VPC for lower latency and simpler routing.
- Ownership: Kyra network team will own peering setup and firewall changes; I'll be the main point for network config.
- Questions:
  * Do you support provision of a small set of static egress IPs (for our allow-lists) or do we need to rely on AWS NAT?
  * Any requirement for BGP or dynamic routing? We prefer static routes if possible.

Available windows for a technical deep dive next week: Mon/Tue 09:00–12:00 PT, Wed 13:00–16:00 PT.

Ellen (cc) will coordinate internal approvals.

-Rajiv

Hi Rajiv / Ellen —

Thanks for the quick note. Short answers up front:
- Static egress IPs: We can allocate up to 3 stable egress IPs for customer allow-lists in the Hosted/Dedicated flow. For Private/VPC peering you would use your AWS NAT or a small AGW we provide; we can document the IPs in the runbook.
- BGP: Not required for the initial rollout. We support static routing and a managed VPN option. BGP can be considered for multi-region HA later.

A couple of items we need from your side before the deep dive:
1) CIDR ranges for the Kyra VPC subnets to avoid overlap with our dedicated VPC (please include test and prod ranges).
2) Firewall/NGFW vendor and any enforced egress proxy requirements.
3) Point-of-contact for on-prem install (if you opt for the on-prem package).

I've attached a filled excerpt of the rdw-onprem-pack-checklist with questions inline (rdw-onprem-pack-checklist.xlsx). Let's take the deep technical dive on Mon 09:30 PT if that works for your team — propose sending a calendar invite for 60 mins.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Introductions — OptiNet integrations (runbook + SLA)

Hi all —

Samir here from OptiNet, the integrator Kyra selected for firewall and on-prem orchestration. I'll be supporting the cutover and firewall rule changes. Attaching our standard optinet-sla.pdf and a short runbook template.

For coordination: we typically do a 30–45 minute runbook read-through with Dev + Rajiv to confirm ports, NAT, and the cutover window. We're available Tue/Wed afternoons PT.

A couple of notes from our pre-checks on your diagram:
- We see a stateful NGFW in front of the application subnet — we'll need an allow-list for the three egress IPs and a small set of inbound rules for management (SSH/HTTPS) from our maintenance IPs.
- If you plan to host the KV cache behind an internal network segment, share those subnets and we'll validate routes.

Best,
Samir Shah
Principal Engineer, Integrations
